registered.recorded_by: Claude Code F-3d v4 pre-registration (Fable 5.1 workflow, scripts/70)
registered.statement: The v4 rule (template set, reader options, thresholds and the A-10 acceptance criterion) was fixed after every 1st-5th inning eval-set frame (142 pitches, PA 1-40) and every negatives frame (14) had been seen and their v1-v3 results and failure causes diagnosed (F-3c comparison, the 34/3 misread register entry, the F-3d design/judge scratch under outputs/verification/f3d/), and before any 6th-inning frame was annotated or looked at. Nothing measured on those frames is held-out, blind or generalisation evidence for v4; it is development evidence. The first blind evaluation of v4 is the A-10 6th-inning new-row comparison (PA 41-49), judged by acceptance_criterion_for_A10 below.

amendments.stage: F-3d repair round, before the pre-registration was committed
changes: Criterion (4): dropped the unsatisfiable requirement that the v1-v3 predictions and score files be byte-identical after the A-10 merge (the refresh appends the new rows to every version and recomputes coverage counts); byte-identity now applies to the v1-v3 template and negatives files, and the predictions/score files are checked through changed_shared_rows 0 / removed_rows 0 / parsed_documents_equal.

Criterion (4): the clause 'v1-v3 wrong reads are exactly the registered 34/3 topbot' now applies to the 142 shared rows only; what the frozen v1-v3 read on the PA 41-49 rows is outside v4's control and does not decide v4's pass/fail.

Criterion (4): the anchor is the committed v4 predictions file (LF-normalised sha256 and git blob id recorded), not the git-ignored design scratch file; equality with that scratch file on all 142 rows is recorded as a registration-time fact.

Criterion (5): the per-glyph evidence now comes from `scripts/66 predict --diagnostics` (added in this round; predict printed only counts before), and the balls/strikes clause excludes gate-failing rows and no-glyph windows explicitly, as the inning_topbot clause already did.

files_as_built: hashes are LF-normalised sha256 (plus git blob ids) so that they verify on LF checkouts (CI, macOS/Linux); the earlier hashes were of the CRLF working-tree bytes of one Windows machine.

acceptance_helper: new_rows_acceptance now also takes the wrong_reads list over all candidate rows and reports valid=false when a baseline block covers other pitches; validate_reader_options rejects a non-finite topbot_rule.min_slope and a null min_margin_by_field is treated as absent on the read path.
amendments.unchanged: Template set, reader option values, thresholds, criteria (1)-(3), the v4 template, prediction, score and negatives files (byte-identical to the first build; rerun via scripts/70 in the repair round) and the development-set numbers.

template_rule: v4 source plate appearances = exactly {1, 2, 9, 18, 29}, the v3 set; nothing added or removed (no 5th-inning PA, so inning '5' stays untemplated and every 5th-inning row stays outside the template set). Glyphs are cut exactly as in v1-v3: `scripts/66_sny_scoreboard_ocr.py templates` mode, `glyphs_for_label` with the default `segment_glyphs` on the cached decision frames outputs/frames/evalset_<frame_seconds .2f>.jpg of every eval-set entry of those PAs, confirmed DIGIT_FIELDS only (85 fields used, 0 skipped), reader options never applied at cut time; each glyph normalised to 16x12 and stored pooled digit -> list (0:45, 1:14, 2:18, 3:2, 4:6), TEMPLATE_SCHEMA sny_digit_templates_v0, glyph_shape [16, 12]. Build command: `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 uv run --frozen python scripts/66_sny_scoreboard_ocr.py templates --template-pas 1 2 9 18 29 --no-grab --reader-options '{"top_line_gate": {"aggregate": "max_row", "threshold": 0.6}, "border_sliver_max_width": 2, "min_margin_by_field": {"balls": 0.1, "strikes": 0.1}, "arrow_window": [262, 46, 279, 64], "topbot_rule": {"method": "blob_slope", "min_slope": 0.4, "min_rows": 6}}' --output docs/results/mlb_p0/sny_digit_templates_v4.json`. Mechanical check after the build: the `templates` key of the v4 file must equal the `templates` key of sny_digit_templates_v3.json (the judge verified that the same command with only the v3 options reproduces the v3 file as an equal document), and `source.template_plate_appearances` must be [1, 2, 9, 18, 29].
template_build_command: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 uv run --frozen python scripts/66_sny_scoreboard_ocr.py templates --template-pas 1 2 9 18 29 --no-grab --reader-options '{"top_line_gate": {"aggregate": "max_row", "threshold": 0.6}, "border_sliver_max_width": 2, "min_margin_by_field": {"balls": 0.1, "strikes": 0.1}, "arrow_window": [262, 46, 279, 64], "topbot_rule": {"method": "blob_slope", "min_slope": 0.4, "min_rows": 6}}' --output docs/results/mlb_p0/sny_digit_templates_v4.json

reader_options_semantics.name: top_line_gate
reader_options_semantics.semantics: Unchanged from v3: the top-line presence test passes when any single row of the top_line window reaches the threshold.
reader_options_semantics.validation: Existing validate_reader_options rules (aggregate in TOP_LINE_AGGREGATES, threshold a number in [0, 1]).

reader_options_semantics.name: border_sliver_max_width
reader_options_semantics.semantics: Unchanged from v3: a column group at most 2 px wide touching a digit window's edge is dropped before the size tests.

reader_options_semantics.name: min_margin_by_field
reader_options_semantics.semantics: Per-DIGIT_FIELD replacement for MIN_MARGIN. `DigitTemplates.match(glyph, min_margin=MIN_MARGIN)` gains a keyword whose default is today's constant; `read_number(white, name, templates, options)` passes `options.get('min_margin_by_field', {}).get(name, MIN_MARGIN)`. Fields not listed (inning, away_score, home_score) keep 0.15. MAX_DISTANCE 0.12 is untouched, so a probe farther than 0.12 from every template still abstains (13/3 balls, distance 0.1234, stays abstained). Templates stay pooled: the count window still competes against every digit of every font, so the floor is at least as conservative as the same floor on grouped templates.
reader_options_semantics.validation: Must be a JSON object; every key in DIGIT_FIELDS ('balls', 'strikes', 'inning', 'away_score', 'home_score'); every value a number (bool rejected) within [0, 1]. Unknown field names or out-of-range values raise ValueError naming the offending key; absent key = MIN_MARGIN everywhere (v0-v3 behaviour).

reader_options_semantics.name: arrow_window
reader_options_semantics.semantics: Replaces WINDOWS['arrow'] for `read_topbot` only: `read_topbot(white, options=None)` takes `(options or {}).get('arrow_window') or WINDOWS['arrow']` and slices `white[y0:y1, x0:x1]` exactly as `window()` does (x1 exclusive: columns 262-278). The arrow's left edge is x 269 in the 1st inning and 264/265 in innings 2-5 (the arrow+digit block shifts with the inning digit width), so the default x0 266 clips 1-2 columns and the base rows measure 7-9 px; with x0 262 every base row is measured in full. x1 stays 279 because the 5th-inning inning digit's left edge sits at x 278/279 (dropping column 278 was measured and does not help). WINDOWS itself is not edited; `read_scoreboard` forwards the options it already has.
reader_options_semantics.validation: Must be a list of exactly 4 integers (bool rejected) [x0, y0, x1, y1] with 0 <= x0 < x1 <= 1280 and 0 <= y0 < y1 <= 720; anything else raises ValueError naming the option. Absent key = WINDOWS['arrow'] (v0-v3 behaviour).

reader_options_semantics.name: topbot_rule
reader_options_semantics.semantics: Opt-in decision rule inside `read_topbot`, applied to the arrow window (the `arrow_window` option when present, else WINDOWS['arrow']): (1) connected column groups of white pixels (same construction as `segment_glyphs`, but without MIN_GLYPH_WIDTH/HEIGHT and without the sliver option); the widest group (ties: leftmost) is the arrow blob, cropped to its non-empty row span (this drops the inning digit's 1-px left edge at column 278 and any narrower stray); (2) abstain (None) if the blob has fewer than `min_rows` rows; (3) widths = white count per blob row, slope = least-squares slope of width against row index (np.polyfit degree 1 or the closed form); Top if slope >= min_slope (widths grow downward = up arrow), Bot if slope <= -min_slope, else None. Independent of the widest row and of which corner the window clips: clipping scales the widths but not the sign of the trend, and a single-row tie cannot flip a slope. When the key is absent the existing argmax body runs verbatim (widths >= 2, >= 6 rows, widest-row position >= 0.6 Top / <= 0.4 Bot).
reader_options_semantics.validation: Must be a JSON object with `method` == 'blob_slope' (the only method), `min_slope` a number > 0 (bool rejected), `min_rows` an int >= 2 (bool rejected); unknown keys rejected; every violation raises ValueError naming `topbot_rule` and the offending key. Absent key = v0-v3 argmax behaviour.

topbot_rule: blob_slope on the widened window (both opt-in): arrow window x 262-278, y 46-63; largest connected column group = arrow blob; abstain below 6 rows; least-squares slope of the blob's row widths; Top if >= 0.4 px/row, Bot if <= -0.4, else abstain. Measured cause of 34/3 and 37/5: the arrow's left edge is x 264/265 from the 2nd inning on, the default window x0 266 clips it, the base rows measure 7-9 px and JPEG jitter tied four rows at 8 px, so argmax picked the first tied row (34/3 position 0.375 -> Bot, 37/5 0.5 -> abstain). Judge measurements on the 139 confirmed, gate-passing arrows (58 Top, 81 Bot): current argmax 137/1 wrong/1 abstain with 33 of 58 Top frames within 1 px of a tie; argmax at x0 262 139/139 (Top 0.75-0.875, Bot 0.0) but still 14 Top frames within 2 px of a tie and 7 abstentions under 1-px vertical+horizontal dilation, 58 under 2-px vertical dilation, 3 wrong reads under dilation at the current window; blob_slope at x0 262 139/139 clean (Top slopes 0.717-1.267, Bot -1.2..-1.1; lowest Top 29/3 at 0.717, 34/3 reads 1.05, 37/5 reads Top), 139/139 under every 1-px dilation/erosion and 2-px dilation (Top min 0.544, Bot max -0.75), 120/139 under 2-px vertical+horizontal erosion with 0 wrong (the arrow falls below 6 rows and abstains). blob_slope at x0 262 reproduces the pre-registered inning_topbot value on all 142 eval rows (8/1, 16/1, 33/1 abstain via the gate) and on the negatives reads the 4 cutaways Bot (slopes -1.1..-1.167), misses 780 via the gate, 0 false reads. The thirds ratio on the raw window is NOT adopted (17 wrong reads under 1-px horizontal dilation from the inning digit's edge column); the v0-v3 argmax body stays verbatim for documents without `topbot_rule`.
count_2_vs_3_fix: Cause (both designers, same numbers): the count-font '2' probes that abstain (20/5, 20/7, 33/5, 35/5; all 17x11 boxes) sit 0.065-0.081 from the nearest of the 10 count-'2' templates but the templates themselves spread up to 0.148 apart, so against the single count-font '3' template (29/7) at 0.208-0.219 the margin lands at 0.1325-0.1432, below MIN_MARGIN 0.15. The count-font 2 and 3 are not close at 16x12 (template-to-template 0.246-0.30; the 4 count-'3' probes sit 0.0-0.021 from the '3' and >= 0.236 from any '2'), and per-field grouping changes nothing (identical distances to 4 decimals; the pooled runner-up was already the count-font '3'). Fix: opt-in `min_margin_by_field` {"balls": 0.10, "strikes": 0.10} on the unchanged pooled templates, MAX_DISTANCE 0.12 untouched. Evidence: on all 278 count glyphs of the 139 gate-passing frames the best digit equals the label in every case ('0' n=122 margin >= 0.262, '1' n=75 >= 0.292, '2' n=77 with the lowest 0.1155 (13/3, abstains on distance 0.1234 regardless), 0.1325, 0.1325, 0.1432, 0.1432, then 0.1543 and >= 0.1765, '3' n=4 >= 0.214); the floor sweep 0.15/0.13/0.12/0.11/0.10/0.09/0.08/0.06 gives margin abstentions 4/0/0/0/0/0/0/0 and 0 wrong reads at every floor, so the development result does not depend on the exact value; 0.10 is 0.0325 below the lowest accepted margin and 0.10 above the wrong-read boundary. A wrong count read would need a '3' (or '0') template closer than the nearest '2' template while within 0.12, which no count glyph of 278 comes near (runner-up distances >= 0.208). Strikes gets the same floor because it shows the same count font (its lowest '2' margin today is 0.1765). This is honestly a floor lowered after seeing the margins; the robust native matcher (count-2 margins 0.25-0.26 with unchanged thresholds) was rejected because it moves the risk to the distance side (16x5 '1' at 0.100 of 0.12) and costs a second matcher.
acceptance_criterion_for_A10: Fixed now, before the A-10 rows exist. Inputs: the output of `scripts/70_refresh_ocr_reports.py --reference <last commit before the A-10 merge> --no-grab` run for every version at once after the merge, i.e. the `new_rows_comparison` block (totals + per-pitch `wrong_fields` / `abstained_fields` / `evaluable_fields`) of each version's provenance file, its `previous_prediction_comparison`, its negatives score file and `wrong_reads` over all prediction rows. The new rows are the PA 41-49 pitches (34); `new_rows_missing_from_evalset` must be 0 for the check to be valid (otherwise the eval set was not rebuilt and the check is rerun after rebuilding, not judged). v4 PASSES only if ALL hold: (1) v4 `new_rows_comparison.totals.pitches_with_wrong_field` == 0 and `wrong_reads(v4)` over all v4 rows is empty; v4 has no entry in game_747139_scoreboard_known_misreads.json, so any wrong read anywhere fails scripts/70 for v4 and fails this criterion. (2) Per field, for each of the 10 LABEL_FIELDS, correct_v(field) = number of new-row pitches where the field is confirmed (in the entry's field_status) minus those listing it in `abstained_fields` or `wrong_fields`, computed from the per-pitch lists of that version's block; v4 must satisfy correct_v4 >= correct_v2 AND correct_v4 >= correct_v3 for every field. No exclusion clause: a score or count label digit without a template that v2/v3 happen to read and v4 does not counts against v4. The inning field is expected to be 0 correct / 34 abstained for v1-v4 (no '6' template); that is not a failure, but any v4 inning value on a new row is a wrong read and fails (1). (3) v4 negatives `false_reads` == 0 and `wrong_reads` == 0. (4) v4 `previous_prediction_comparison.changed_shared_rows` == 0 and `removed_rows` == 0 against the pre-registered v4 predictions file committed before the merge (docs/results/mlb_p0/game_747139_scoreboard_ocr_v4_predictions.json at the pre-merge commit: 142 PA 1-40 rows, hashes under preregistered_v4_predictions; at registration it equalled the design scratch file on all 142 rows), and v4 `current_repeat_check.parsed_documents_equal` true. Isolation of v1, v2 and v3 (their read paths must not have moved): each reports changed_shared_rows 0, removed_rows 0 and current_repeat_check.parsed_documents_equal true against the pre-merge commit; their template files (sny_digit_templates_v1/v2/v3.json) and their negatives score files are byte-identical to the pre-merge commit; their predictions and score files change only by the addition of the new rows (the A-10 refresh appends the PA 41-49 rows to every version's predictions file and recomputes the score file's coverage counts, so byte-identity is not required of those two files; the shared-row checks establish that nothing else moved). On the 142 shared PA 1-40 rows the v1-v3 wrong reads are exactly the registered 34/3 inning_topbot. What v1-v3 read on the new rows is outside v4's control and does not decide v4's pass/fail: a new v1-v3 misread on a PA 41-49 row is registered as v1-v3 evidence in game_747139_scoreboard_known_misreads.json (versions v1-v3 only) and does not fail (4). (5) Pre-stated field expectations, computed from `scripts/66_sny_scoreboard_ocr.py predict --templates docs/results/mlb_p0/sny_digit_templates_v4.json --diagnostics <path> --no-grab` on the cached A-10 frames (per pitch: `gate_passed`, and per digit field every segmented glyph's best digit, distance, margin, min_margin and read; `digit_field_diagnostics`): v4 inning_topbot on the new rows has 0 wrong and abstains only on pitches whose frame fails the presence gate (gate_passed false, every field None on that row), i.e. no arrow-rule abstention on a gate-passing frame; on gate-passing new rows every v4 balls/strikes abstention is a distance abstention (a segmented glyph of that window has distance > MAX_DISTANCE 0.12) or a no-glyph window (the window's diagnostics list is empty); a margin abstention (every glyph of the window within 0.12 but one with margin < its min_margin) on a gate-passing new row fails (5). Gate-failing rows are excluded from this clause for every field, as for inning_topbot. Any failure of (1)-(5) is reported as a FAILED v4 like v3's failed check; v4 is not re-optioned, re-templated or re-thresholded afterwards, and the PA 41-49 rows are then no longer blind for any successor. Pre-registered expectations that are not pass conditions: v4 reads count digits 0-3 on every gate-passing 6th-inning frame, abstains on inning 34/34, reads Top/Bot on every gate-passing frame, and reads scores only while they consist of the digits 0 and 2.
acceptance_helper: src.vision.ocr_reports.new_rows_acceptance(evalset, v4_block, {'v2': v2_block, 'v3': v3_block}, negatives_totals=<v4 negatives score totals>, wrong_reads=ocr_reports.wrong_reads(evalset, <all v4 prediction rows>)) evaluates criteria (1)-(3) in full from the new_rows_comparison blocks of the provenance files written by scripts/70 after the A-10 merge: both halves of (1) (new-row wrong fields and wrong reads over all v4 rows), the per-field rule (2) and the negatives rule (3). It reports valid=false (never a pass) when new_rows_missing_from_evalset > 0 or when a baseline block covers other pitches than the candidate block. (4) is checked from previous_prediction_comparison / current_repeat_check and the byte-compare of the v1-v3 template and negatives files; (5) from the `predict --diagnostics` dump, as the criterion states.

preregistered_v4_predictions.note: This committed file is what criterion (4) compares against after the A-10 merge (changed_shared_rows must be 0 on these 142 rows). Its equality with the git-ignored design scratch file outputs/verification/f3d/minimal/predictions_v4_pooled_margin_window.json was verified at registration and again in the repair round; the committed file, not the scratch file, is the anchor.

files_as_built_hashing: sha256 of the file bytes with CRLF line endings normalised to LF (this repository checks out CRLF on Windows under core.autocrlf while git, CI and macOS/Linux clones hold LF; the hashes verify on every checkout). files_as_built_git_blob_sha1 is `git hash-object <path>` with the clean filter applied, i.e. the blob id `git rev-parse <commit>:<path>` shows at the registered commit. Only the sny_digit_templates_v4.json hash is pinned by a test (tests/test_sny_scoreboard.py); the source hashes (src/vision/sny_scoreboard.py, scripts/66_sny_scoreboard_ocr.py) and the prediction/score/negatives hashes are a registration-time record to verify against the registered commit's blobs, because successors edit the sources and the A-10 refresh appends rows to the prediction and score files.

criterion_5_form_on_the_development_set.note: DEVELOPMENT evidence (every frame seen): scripts/66 predict --diagnostics with the v4 template file over the 142 PA 1-40 rows, classified as criterion (5) will classify the A-10 rows.

v1_v3_isolation.statement: v1, v2, v3 template files, predictions, scores, negatives and provenance files are not touched (only scripts/70 writes provenance refreshes of its own). Code changes are strictly additive and keyed on option presence: READER_OPTION_KEYS extended with 'min_margin_by_field', 'arrow_window', 'topbot_rule' and validate_reader_options extended with their checks (v1/v2 files have no reader_options, the v3 file carries only its two keys, so their validated dicts are unchanged); `DigitTemplates.match(glyph, min_margin=MIN_MARGIN)` with the default equal to today's constant; `read_number` reads the per-field floor only from `options` (absent -> MIN_MARGIN); `read_topbot(white, options=None)` uses WINDOWS['arrow'] when `arrow_window` is absent and runs the existing argmax body verbatim when `topbot_rule` is absent; `read_scoreboard` only forwards the options it already has. WINDOWS, MAX_DISTANCE, MIN_MARGIN, GLYPH_SHAPE, MIN_GLYPH_WIDTH/HEIGHT, masks, FILLED/EMPTY, presence-gate constants, TEMPLATE_SCHEMA and every function default stay as they are; templates are still cut with the default segmentation. Verification before claiming v4: (a) run scripts/70 for --version v1 v2 v3 into outputs/verification/f3d/v123_before (pre-change) and outputs/verification/f3d/v1v3 (post-change) with --skip-provenance and byte-compare predictions, score and negatives files, plus sha256 of sny_digit_templates_v1/v2/v3.json unchanged (the f3c procedure); (b) `scripts/check_project.py --cpu-only` stays green (335 passed + new tests); (c) new tests in tests/test_sny_scoreboard.py: a v3-options document produces predictions identical to the committed v3 file on cached frames (extend test_reader_options_absent_or_empty_is_the_default_path / test_stored_heldout_score_excludes_its_template_plate_appearances to v4); validate_reader_options rejects a malformed min_margin_by_field (unknown field, value 1.5, bool), arrow_window (3 items, x0 >= x1, bool) and topbot_rule (unknown method, min_slope 0, min_rows 1, unknown key) each with a ValueError naming the option; a synthetic-frame test that read_topbot without options returns Bot on a clipped up arrow with tied base rows while read_topbot with the v4 arrow_window + topbot_rule returns Top, and that a synthetic down arrow returns Bot under both; a test that a v3-layout document loaded and re-serialised keeps its key order and no new keys. The known-misread register keeps versions v1-v3 for 34/3; v4 is not added because it does not make that read.
v1_v3_isolation.verification_2026_09_25: scripts/70 --version v1/v2/v3 --reference HEAD --skip-provenance --no-grab run before the change (outputs/verification/f3d/v123_before) and, after the change and again after the repair round, into outputs/verification/f3d/v1v3: all nine predictions/score/negatives files byte-identical to the committed files; sha256 of sny_digit_templates_v1/v2/v3.json unchanged; git diff shows no v1-v3 file changed.

risks: All numbers are development evidence: the four balls-'2' fixes and the two topbot fixes were made after those exact frames were diagnosed; the margin floor 0.10 was chosen after seeing margins of 0.1325-0.1432 (the sweep 0.06-0.13 limits but does not remove the tuning); the slope threshold 0.4 was set with the dev-set Top minimum 0.633/0.717 in view. Nothing is held-out; the A-10 rows are the first blind test and only for the 6th-inning content they contain.

No count glyph in the dev set has a wrong best digit, so the lower bound of a safe count margin is unmeasured; a blurred count glyph within 0.12 of a wrong template with margin >= 0.10 would be read wrong. MAX_DISTANCE 0.12 is the remaining guard and the 2-vs-3 decision rests on a single count-font '3' template (4 probes seen).

Inning '6' has no template; v4 abstains only if the '6' glyph is > 0.12 from every 0-4 template or its pooled margin < 0.15. The inning '5' proxy sits at 0.23 from its nearest template with margin 0.06-0.08, which suggests but does not prove the same for '6' (a '6' resembling '0' more than a '5' does). A '6' read as any digit is a wrong read and fails the criterion. The 5th-inning inning glyph starts at x 278/279, one or two columns left of the inning window, so a wider '6' would be clipped there.

The arrow rule assumes the arrow is the widest connected column group in x 262-278, y 46-63 on gate-passing frames; a graphic that places a wider white shape there while the presence gate passes would be read Top/Bot. Foreign white at x 262-265 was absent on every gate-passing frame seen, but that is 139 frames of one broadcast layout; the arrow's position depends on the inning digit width (269 in inning 1, 264/265 in innings 2-5), and a '6' of unusual width could move it (clip margin 2 px; the slope rule tolerates clipping, the window widening only makes the statistic cleaner).

Pooled templates keep cross-font recall but also mean every new template lowers other fields' margins; if the score changes in the 6th inning, a score-font '1' or '3' is matched through count/inning templates with unmeasured distances, and the strict per-field rule (no exclusion clause) can then fail v4 through an abstention where v2 reads by luck. That is accepted so that the criterion cannot be softened after the fact.

The `score --exclude-pas 1 2 9 18 29` set for v4 contains 0 held-out pitches today; the v4 SCORE_SET_NOTES entry and this pre-registration file (there is no separate v4 comparison file) must say so, and the v4 all-fields number (93/122) must never be presented as a held-out result.
The topbot_rule branch is new code on the read path (about 15 lines); its default-off behaviour is guaranteed only by the v1-v3 byte-compare and the new synthetic tests listed under v1_v3_isolation.
